label.trigger: A wheel contains a member whose name climbs one level and re-enters a sibling folder that starts with the same characters as the scheme folder, e.g. ../purelib-extra/planted.py while purelib maps to /prefix/purelib, and it is installed through SchemeDictionaryDestination.
label.expected_impact: After normalisation the member resolves to /prefix/purelib-extra/planted.py. The containment test compares the two paths as plain strings, and that string begins with /prefix/purelib, so the escape is accepted and write_to_fs creates a file in a neighbouring directory chosen by the archive author (and replaces an existing one there when overwrite_existing is enabled).

anchors.end: f"Attempting to write {path} outside of the target directory"

context_locations.note: The install loop takes each name straight from the wheel's record entries and hands it, possibly unchanged for root-scheme files, to destination.write_file, so the name is attacker data when it reaches the guard.
Member names come from the zip directory itself and are not normalised or screened for parent segments here.
The sink: whatever path the guard lets through has its parents created and is opened for writing.

known_counterevidence.note: Escapes that land somewhere not sharing the scheme folder's name prefix are still refused, so the project test passes; only sibling names that extend the folder name get through.
This commonpath comparison only routes members into the right scheme; it is component based and is not the place of the defect.

label.fix_summary: Compare path components instead of characters, for example by going back to the pathlib is_relative_to method or by using os.path.commonpath, so that a neighbour such as purelib-extra no longer counts as being inside purelib.

check.summary: Independent pytest module copied into the work copy: it builds a SchemeDictionaryDestination under a temporary prefix and asks write_file to store members that climb into purelib-extra, purelibs and purelib2, expecting ValueError and no planted file; two control tests cover a normal member and a plain parent escape.

verification.summary: verify --run-checks with system Python 3.14.4 and pytest 9.0.2: on before the three sibling-prefix cases of the added module fail (no ValueError is raised and the member is written) while the controls and the project's tests/test_destinations.py pass; on after all 16 tests pass. PYTHONPATH is the work copy's src directory; the project has no runtime dependencies. The existing project test alone does not detect the seeded change, which is why the independent module is used.
